articles.name: Release notes through 2026-09-18
articles.title: Release notes through 2026-09-18
articles.body:
See the What's New section for an overview of last month's releases.

This week's release notes include:

  • Admin Center
  • AI Agents
  • Copilot
  • Contact Center
  • Zendesk QA
  • Apps and integrations
  • Products with no updates this week

Admin Center

New:

  • The audit log events for creating and deleting OAuth tokens now show the OAuth client name in the Activity column

AI Agents

New:

  • Agentic email
    • As of September 16, 2026, all agentic email customers have access to new functionality for creating and using embedded templates in generative procedures, providing parity with the messaging channel.
  • Web crawler

    • Web crawler locale-handling updates are rolling out to better align crawled content with the locales configured for each help center.

      The rollout includes improved locale-filtering behavior and updated product guidance. See Understanding web crawler locales. The rollout is ongoing.

Fixed:

  • Agentic Email
    • Now completes the reply as expected when the AI agent's procedure finishes successfully.
    • Email turns that were failing to process now complete successfully.
  • Web Crawler
    • More reliable sitemap crawling. Fixed an issue that could prevent sitemap URLs from being discovered and crawled successfully. Web Crawler now handles sitemap depth separately from page-crawl depth, improving support for nested sitemaps.
    • Improved URL filtering. Web Crawler now filters start URLs marked as no-follow before fetching them. This reduces unnecessary requests and helps prevent unintended crawling.
    • Clearer crawler setup guidance. Improved the crawler creation experience with clearer start-URL labels and format guidance. Also fixed an untranslated example URL in localized crawler setup flows.
    • Improved error handling. Improved handling of product-limit connection errors so API clients receive more accurate error responses.

Copilot

New:

  • Similar tickets show agents past tickets that resemble the one they're working on, so they can apply proven solutions instead of starting from scratch. By reusing what already worked for that scenario, your agents can reduce average handling time and deliver faster, more consistent answers to customers. See Turning on similar tickets.

Contact Center

New:

Contact Center App

  • Upgraded Streams to 2.29.1 and ChatJS to 5.1.1 for improved stability across chat and voice calls.

Fixed:

Contact Center App

  • Improved onboarding for accounts using OAuth by enabling users to set the userId configuration field.
  • Fixed an issue where pressing Enter in the external search field caused the app to reload. 

Zendesk QA

New:

  • On September 21, 2026, we're updating the AI model for QA custom prompt evaluations. Review your prompts after this date to ensure outputs meet your expectations.
  • Restricted visibility of AutoQA score for Agents inside Zendesk QA
  • Zendesk QA HUB for easy QA set up and onboarding

Apps and integrations

New:
  • ZenTennis (Support)
    • ZenTennis gives support agents a playful break inside the Zendesk ticket sidebar. Agents play a first-to-five botanical rally, with configurable difficulty and keyboard, pointer, or on-screen controls. Administrators can optionally track completed results in the ticket.
  • Ticket Nibbler (Support)
    • Ticket Nibbler is a compact arcade-style break game in the ticket sidebar. Agents guide a growing worm around the board, eating plants while avoiding walls and its own body. It supports multiple control methods, configurable speed, and optional score tracking on tickets.
  • Refundid Returns and Exchanges (Support)
    • Refundid lets support agents see a customer's recent Refundid returns and refunds directly on the ticket, including references, order information, status, resolution, items, tracking, and shipping-label details. Agents can also search by order number or email and link into the Refundid merchant dashboard.
  • VendorApp Admin (Support)
    • VendorApp Admin embeds the VendorApp administration console inside Zendesk Support. It is designed for B2B2B and B2B2C support environments where vendors, partners, and customers need isolated branded portals while tickets, organizations, and users remain in Zendesk. The app provides in-Zendesk administration for portals, organizations, users, branding, and the Zendesk connection.
  • GrowOn Note Taker (Support)
    • GrowOn Note Taker lets agents create, edit, and delete ticket-specific working notes from the Zendesk sidebar without adding them to the ticket conversation. Notes remain associated with the ticket and retain creator and timestamp context. The app stores its note data in the customer's Zendesk account using Custom Objects.
  • SOCRadar Alert Management (Support)
    • SOCRadar Alert Management integrates SOCRadar's Extended Threat Intelligence platform with Zendesk Support. It can poll for new security alarms, create tickets automatically, display incidents in a dashboard, and let agents manage alarm status, severity, and comments from Zendesk. It supports multiple alarm categories including attack-surface, vulnerability, dark-web, brand-protection, fraud, threat-hunting, and supply-chain intelligence.
  • Refaire (Support)
    • Refaire is an AI-powered remote visual support platform that helps customers troubleshoot issues with their phone camera before human support is needed. When escalation occurs, it creates a Zendesk ticket containing diagnostic context such as attempted fixes, outcomes, product information, photos, and video. Agents can continue the support interaction in Zendesk and escalate according to configurable rules.
  • Data Custodian (Support) (paid)
    • Data Custodian lets you search the whole account with exact counts, export tickets with comments to CSV, Excel or JSON, change or delete thousands of tickets with undo, redact personal data, answer access requests with a complete pack, forget a person, run retention rules after a dry run. Every action leaves evidence.
  • Help Center Doctor (Support) (paid)

    • Help Center Doctor is a Zendesk app that scans and repairs help center content entirely within the customer’s browser. It checks articles and translations for issues such as broken links, missing alt text, stale or duplicate content, empty sections, and outdated translations. Key features include bulk fixes, find-and-replace, article editing, document exports, templates, snippets, and a link map. Changes are previewed, backed up locally, and reversible.

  • Help Center Article Templates (Support) (paid)

    • Help Center Article Templates helps Zendesk teams create help center articles without starting from scratch. It provides built-in templates for formats such as how-to guides, FAQs, troubleshooting articles, release notes, policies, product overviews, and announcements, along with reusable content snippets. Users can create custom templates, use fill-in placeholders, select sections, labels, languages, and permissions, and generate unpublished drafts directly in Zendesk. Pro users also get shared team libraries, multilingual drafts, publishing checklists, and JSON import/export.

  • Help Center Print & Export (Support) (paid)
    • Help Center Print & Export lets Zendesk users export any portion of their help center—individual articles, sections, categories, or the entire knowledge base—into professional documents without leaving Zendesk or using an external server. Users can filter and select content, choose a language, customize document formatting and branding, preview the results, and export them as PDFs, Word files, HTML, Markdown, ZIP folders, or CSV indexes. Export profiles and history make recurring documents and backups easy to repeat.
  • Help Center Find & Replace (Support) (paid)
    • Help Center Find & Replace lets Zendesk teams search and replace text, links, images, and HTML across all help center articles and languages. It supports plain-text and regular-expression searches, detailed filters, previews, diffs, and per-translation approval. Before making changes, it creates downloadable snapshots, reports progress and errors, and allows users to undo completed runs or restore snapshots. Saved searches simplify recurring rebrands and cleanups. The app also respects Zendesk permissions, warns about content blocks, and manages API requests within rate limits.
  • Help Center Link Checker (Support)
    • Help Center Link Checker scans every article and language to identify broken or problematic links and images. It detects missing, archived, draft, restricted, or outdated internal links, broken anchors, old-domain links, HTTP links, and external URLs or images that fail validation. It checks external resources through Zendesk’s proxy, distinguishes confirmed failures from unverified results, and provides a link map showing which articles reference a given article. Findings include explanations and direct links to the article editor, while repeat scans only recheck changed content.
  • Proactive Outreach (Support) (paid)
    • Proactive Outreach lets Zendesk Support teams send proactive messages to many customers by creating one ticket per recipient. It supports audiences built from users, organizations, matching tickets, or CSV files, with deduplication and extensive exclusions. Messages can use personalized placeholders, macros, previews, language variants, and customizable ticket settings. The app includes test tickets, opt-out handling, configurable delivery limits, pausing and resuming, retry support, and duplicate prevention. Campaign reports track delivery, failures, replies, and opt-outs, with ticket links and CSV export. Saved audiences, templates, and campaign history make recurring outreach easier.

Products with no updates this week

  • Support
  • Knowledge
  • Voice
  • Analytics
  • Zendesk Workforce Management (WFM)
  • Mobile SDKs

articles.name: Error: AADSTS90015: Requested Query string is too long
articles.title: Error: AADSTS90015: Requested Query string is too long
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

Using SSO (Single Sign-On) and Microsoft, I see this error: AADSTS90015: Requested Query string is too long. How can I solve this?

Root cause

Input validation for a http listener has the limit of 4096 bytes and strings, which exceeds the AADSTS90015 limit. This is an issue on the Microsoft end, not from Zendesk.

Resolution steps

To overcome the issue:

  1. Clear your browser cookies, for example on Microsoft Edge and in Chrome
  2. For SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language), some applications send a long Relay State. However, SAML standard stipulate that the Relaystate value must not exceed 80 bytes in length. The permanent solution on the issue would be to ask the application vendor to shorten the request
Disclaimer: Zendesk provides this tutorial for instructional purposes only. Zendesk can't provide support for third-party technologies such as Microsoft. If the above article doesn't help, try searching for a solution online or contact Microsoft.

articles.name: Can I install multiple Web Widgets on the same web page?
articles.title: Can I install multiple Web Widgets on the same web page?
articles.body:
Question

Can I install multiple Web Widgets on the same web page?

Answer

No, installing more than one messaging Web Widget on the same exact page is not recommended by Zendesk. This poses several issues with storage and authentication.

  • Instead, only install a single Web Widget per page

articles.name: Scheduled Maintenance - Oct 13 ~ Oct 20, 2026 | All Pods | Advanced Action Flows, Analytics, Chat, Contact Center, Sales, Support, and Sunshine Conversations - Database upgrade
articles.title: Scheduled Maintenance - Oct 13 ~ Oct 20, 2026 | All Pods | Advanced Action Flows, Analytics, Chat, Contact Center, Sales, Support, and Sunshine Conversations - Database upgrade
articles.body:
Zendesk will perform scheduled database maintenance between October 13 and Oct 20, 2026 as part of a critical version upgrade to the “AWS Aurora” software. This will affect database clusters in all Zendesk regions and Advanced Action Flows, Analytics, Chat, Contact Center, Sales, Support, and Sunshine Conversations products between the dates previously mentioned, with different Pods affected in assigned timings listed below.

These changes will be rolled out through a phased implementation during the allotted maintenance periods. The six-hour windows include preparation, validation, database switchover, and monitoring. They are not expected to represent six hours of continuous customer-visible downtime.
 

Affected features

Impact is limited to specific features that depend on the Aurora database cluster being upgraded. A full Zendesk outage is not expected.

Affected features may include:

  • Action Flows and Custom Actions
  • Notifications
  • Omnichannel Routing and Chat and Messaging Routing
  • Messaging ticket creation and message brokering
  • Messaging and Messaging Triggers
  • Agent Tasks
  • Auto Assist, Intelligent Triage, Enhance Writing for Agents, and Ticket Summary
  • Jira Integration
  • Sell records and activities
  • Legacy Custom Objects
  • Ticket and Messaging attachments
  • Audit and access logs
  • Messaging Tickets Live Metrics
  • Estimated Wait Time

The exact impact depends on the pod, database cluster, and features used by the account. Features that do not depend on the affected Aurora cluster are expected to operate normally.

Customers affected

Customers with data in the affected pods who use the features listed above may experience brief, feature-specific disruption during the relevant maintenance window. Customers may use Zendesk normally outside the window that applies to their pod and affected features.

Maintenance schedule

Times below are shown in UTC and representative local time zones. UTC is the source of truth for the schedule.


Expected behavior

During the relevant maintenance window, customers may experience intermittent errors or performance degradation in specific affected features. The customer-visible interruption is expected to be 20-30 seconds per affected service during the final database switchover.

Customers may experience:

  • Requests in progress failing or being interrupted and requiring a retry
  • Delays in Action Flows, notifications, integrations, messaging ticket creation, message brokering, or background processing
  • Delayed or temporarily unavailable ticket, chat, and message routing
  • Messaging Triggers, Agent Tasks, live metrics, or Estimated Wait Time temporarily failing or showing stale information
  • Temporary failures in AI-assisted features, including Auto Assist, Intelligent Triage, Enhance Writing for Agents, and Ticket Summary
  • Temporary degradation of Jira linking or field synchronisation
  • Attachment uploads or downloads requiring a retry
  • Temporary unavailability of some Sell operations, including saving or logging activities

Routing and background processing are expected to recover after the switchover, but some work may be delayed. Customers should retry requests that fail during the switchover.

What do customers need to do?

Customers do not need to take any action before the maintenance. If a request fails during the relevant window, retry it after the switchover completes.

Contact Zendesk Support if a feature does not recover after the maintenance window or if the behavior continues outside the scheduled window.

What is not affected?

  • This is not a full Zendesk outage.
  • The six-hour maintenance windows are not expected to be periods of continuous downtime.
  • Features and services that do not depend on the affected Aurora cluster are expected to operate normally.
  • Customers outside the affected pod and feature cohort are not expected to be affected.

Why are we doing this?

Zendesk is upgrading the Aurora MySQL database engine to maintain platform security, reliability, and continued AWS support.

articles.name: Multi-intent AI agent conversations caused the same repeated breakdown
articles.title: Multi-intent AI agent conversations caused the same repeated breakdown
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

Multi-intent email AI agent conversations triggered three procedures (IncludedProducts, BookedExtras, and OptionalLocalProducts), but this caused the response to repeat the full breakdown multiple times. Instead, how can I combine them into a single, cohesive answer?

Root cause

Each procedure was attempting to retrieve and answer all three intents rather than only its assigned parameter.

Resolution steps

As a solution:

  1. Update each generative procedure > Agent instructions
  2. Ask the procedure to fetch and answer only its specific parameter, with an explicit prohibition against retrieving other details in the instruction

articles.name: How can I add hyperlinks in the bot responses?
articles.title: How can I add hyperlinks in the bot responses?
articles.body:
Question

Can I add embedded hyperlinks in the bot response and messaging?

Answer

Yes, the Agentic AI agent responses will cite hyperlinks of your active help center, as well as external knowledge sources you connected for your customers. However:

  • As a default behavior, cited hyperlinks only appear after the end user clicks Source in the conversation and Web Widget.

  • If you have a developer, as a workaround, use the messaging Web Widget API and the Set Customization parameter to customize the presentation of the Source. With API, can select one of these three options: Button (default), Bullet list or Numbered list.

    Disclaimer: This article is provided for instructional purposes only. Zendesk does not support or guarantee API code. Post any issues you have in the comments section or try searching for a solution online.

articles.name: Why is my AI agent branch step behaving unpredictably or skipping steps?
articles.title: Why is my AI agent branch step behaving unpredictably or skipping steps?
articles.body:
Question

Why is my AI agent branch step behaving unpredictably or skipping steps?

Answer

This usually happens when a data type mismatch occurs—such as a system variable returning a boolean (true/false) when your branch condition is expecting specific text values (strings like "yes" or "no"). Without a default catch-all route, the AI agent cannot reliably evaluate the condition and may fail silently or produce unintended outputs.

How to Fix it

To make your flow deterministic and prevent unhandled logic errors:

  1. Add a Fallback ("Else") Branch: Ensure every conditional or Switch step has an "Else" / Default path configured. This acts as a safety net to route users predictably whenever a variable is missing, empty, or returns an unexpected format.
  2. Align Data Types: Verify that your variable values match the condition's expected inputs:
    1. If checking for text: Ensure the incoming data produces exact string matches (e.g., "yes_active_order" instead of a raw boolean false).
    2. If checking for booleans: Configure the branch condition to explicitly evaluate true/false flags directly.
  3. Test Mismatched Data Routes: Simulate scenarios where external data or API payloads fail, return null, or yield boolean flags to confirm the Fallback branch triggers as intended.

articles.name: Unable to find the ticket ID in a conversation log
articles.title: Unable to find the ticket ID in a conversation log
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

Upon checking the conversation logs, user is unable to find the ticket ID from the details section of a particular conversation.

Root cause

The ticket ID is not available in the conversation logs for a conversation that has the unassisted status.

Resolution steps

The ticket IDs are not present for all conversations that have the unassisted status from the past 30 days.

Conversations with the unassisted status indicate there was no substantial interaction between the AI agent and end user. This is expected behavior.

articles.name: Automatic translation is missing or unavailable in the settings menu of an existing Zendesk AI agent
articles.title: Automatic translation is missing or unavailable in the settings menu of an existing Zendesk AI agent
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

Automatic translation is missing or unavailable in the settings menu of an existing Zendesk AI agent, despite the account being migrated to Zendesk Agent Workspace/ZOS.

Root cause

The AI agent was created using an older/legacy AI agent creation flow. Automatic translation features are exclusively tied to AI agents created through the modern onboarding creation flow.

Resolution steps

Create a new AI agent using the standard onboarding flow and reconfigure it from scratch.

  • Rebuilding from Scratch: Build a fresh AI agent using the updated creation wizard. This ensures full compatibility with automatic translations.
  • Duplicating Existing AI Agents: While duplicating a functional sandbox AI agent may temporarily retain automatic translation settings, this approach is unsupported for legacy production instances. Creating a brand-new AI agent is the required path forward to ensure long-term stability and full feature access.

articles.name: My AI agent recognizes a single question as two separate intents
articles.title: My AI agent recognizes a single question as two separate intents
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

The bot recognizes a single query or question as two separate intents. For example:

  • A customer asked my AI agent: "I need information on my status. Please connect me to customer support".
  • This then triggers a response for both the status and an escalation flow for customer support in parallel.
  • Finally, this is causing the escalation reply to be followed by a knowledge reply.

How can I resolve this?

Root cause

The AI agent is currently interpreting the message as containing two intents at the same time:

  • a knowledge request about a status
  • a request to connect to customer support

In the situation above, the escalation response can appear before or alongside the knowledge response.

Resolution steps

To resolve this:

  1. Create a new instruction in your AI agent to refine the phrasing of your replies. Your instruction could look like this: If the user message includes both a question and a request to escalate, first answer the question, then ask if they still want to be connected to a human. Don’t escalate immediately when multiple intents are present.
  2. Apply the instruction.
  3. Review your conversational flow and intent configurations one last time.
  4. Finally, refresh the page, and test your AI agent.

articles.name: How can I map custom user fields with Azure?
articles.title: How can I map custom user fields with Azure?
articles.body:
Question

How can I map custom fields with Azure?

Answer

Use the below guide to map custom user fields in Azure Auto-Provisioning to custom user fields in Zendesk.

  1. Go to the Zendesk enterprise app in Azure. Under Manage provisioning, click Edit attribute mappings.
  2. Expand the Mapping section and click Provision Azure Active Directory Users
  3. Select Show advanced options
  4. Click Review your schema here
  5. Download the schema file and make a copy of it as a backup before you make any modifications
  6. Open the schema file in a plain text editor and search for user_fields.department

  7. Find the key value of the custom user field in Zendesk

  8. Add a new entry for this custom user field into the schema list. From the user_fields.department string, replace department with the field key from the previous step.
  9. Copy the modified schema back into the Azure portal. Click Save and refresh your browser.
  10. Navigate back to the attribute Mapping section and add a new one. Select the Zendesk attribute as a destination for the Azure attribute.
Disclaimer: This article is provided for instructional purposes only. Zendesk does not support or guarantee third-party websites. If you cannot follow these steps, try searching for a solution online or reach out to the provider directly.

articles.name: My articles are open to everyone, but don't show in my AI agents if customers aren't logged in
articles.title: My articles are open to everyone, but don't show in my AI agents if customers aren't logged in
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

With AI agents and Knowledge, everything is working as expected when the end user is logged in. Relevant knowledge articles are being returned for the query. However, when my customer is logged out and asks the same query, the AI agent does not provide an answer or return Knowledge articles. 

Root cause

It's possible you connected your content as an external knowledge source. If the viewing permission for your external content connection in Knowledge is set to Only visible to selected user segments (such as Agents and admins or Signed-in users), the AI agent will not surface that content when customers are logged out.

Resolution steps

In Knowledge admin, click Manage articles in the sidebar, then navigate to External content > Connections. Click the options menu next to the relevant connection and select Manage. Under Viewing permissions, select Visible to everyone and click Save.

For complete details on adjusting external content permissions, see Managing external knowledge connections.

articles.name: Both AI agent and email bot are jumping into a conversation that has already been handled by a human agent
articles.title: Both AI agent and email bot are jumping into a conversation that has already been handled by a human agent
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

The AI agent and email bot are jumping into a conversation that has already been handled by a human agent.

There's no "Escalation to agent" event or an "Escalated by ultimate" tag indicated in the conversation log.

Resolution steps

This scenario does not sound plausible but here's how you can verify this issue: 

  1. Verify the conversation logs and look for any evidence that the conversation was escalated to the human agent.

  2. In addition, carefully read what triggers an escalation in agentic email AI agents to understand the possible root cause

  3. Then, make amendments to the root cause

articles.name: Which Zendesk API endpoints can I use to extract AI agent conversations?
articles.title: Which Zendesk API endpoints can I use to extract AI agent conversations?
articles.body:
Question

I am building a custom AI assistant. Which Zendesk API endpoints can I use to extract AI agent conversation data?

Answer

To extract AI agent conversation data from Zendesk, you'll need to use these key API endpoints and data fields:

  1. Use the AI agents Data Export API (https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/ai-agents/api/data-export/v3/get-signed-urls) to export conversation records as JSON files.

  2. For full ticket conversation history, use the Ticket Audits API.

  3. To access AI insight fields like topic, sentiment, and language, use the Ticket Fields API. The main custom fields are: Topic, Topic confidence, Sentiment, Sentiment confidence, Language, and Language confidence.

  4. For background ticket generation, create custom ticket fields, get their field names and IDs, and use them in your metadata flow.

  5. For bulk data, consider the Incremental Exports API.

  6. System ticket fields like Priority aren't supported in messaging widget metadata flows.

articles.name: Error: Failed to invoke action. Request failed with status code 404
articles.title: Error: Failed to invoke action. Request failed with status code 404
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

An Action flow is failing in a procedure for tickets and problem tickets with an error code: “Failed to invoke action. Request failed with status code 404”. However, the action executes correctly when tested within the Action Flow builder. What is the issue?

Root cause

The error code 404 during the execution of an action flow, but not in the builder, usually indicates that the agent or flow is trying to invoke an action or integration that isn't found or available in the runtime context, even though it works in testing.

In addition, you may have an action in the procedure that sets the problem ticket id to zendesk_ticket_id:

  • In order for this action to work, the Zendesk ticket must be linked to an existing problem ticket.

  • Since there is no problem ticket associated with the tickets processed by the bot, this action will not save a ticket ID as zendesk_ticket_id. Since there is no ticket id stored in zendesk_ticket_id, the action flow fails and throws a 404 error.

Resolution steps

To resolve this, you may need to:

  1. Consider removing that action

  2. Use the action that sets the platform conversation ID as zendesk_ticket_id instead

  3. Test the procedure to see if your setup works as expected

articles.name: Unable to select the  “Turn on agentic AI” option
articles.title: Unable to select the  “Turn on agentic AI” option
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

I'd like to enable agentic labs and procedures however the option to do so is greyed out.

Root cause

This is an expected behavior because Gen 2 doesn't offer procedures.

Resolution steps

Based on your current configuration, to enable Turn on agentic AI and resolve the issue:

  1. Create a new Advanced email AI agent.

  2. All newly created email AI agents use Agentic AI (Gen 3) by default, so this would provide the Gen 3 capabilities the customer is looking for.

  3. However, if you specifically want to enable Agentic AI on an existing or copied email AI agent, reach out to Zendesk Customer Support. Include the name of the email AI agent the customer would like to migrate to Gen 3. Suggest to raise an escalation with the Zendesk development team to review whether an in-place migration to Gen 3 is possible.

articles.name: Announcing the removal of help center templating APIs v1, v2, and v3
articles.title: Announcing the removal of help center templating APIs v1, v2, and v3
articles.body:
Zendesk is announcing the removal of help center templating APIs v1, v2, and v3. To maintain your help center's functionality and styling, you must upgrade to Templating API v4.

This announcement includes the following sections:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

We're removing the ability to use templating APIs v1, v2, and v3. The transition to v4 will occur in a phased rollout to give you time to migrate your custom themes:

  • September 14, 2026: We will block the import of v1, v2, and v3 themes for all new accounts.
  • November 25, 2026: We will launch the Zendesk Command Line Interface (ZCLI) upgrade tool to assist developers with migrating custom-coded themes.
  • March 1, 2027: We will launch an in-product GUI upgrade tool. At this time, importing v1, v2, and v3 themes will be completely blocked for all accounts.
  • July 31, 2027: All remaining legacy themes will be forcefully upgraded to v4, and v1, v2, and v3 will be completely removed.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

Maintaining four versions of the templating API slows down product development and prevents customers on older versions from accessing new features. By consolidating to API v4, we can:

  • Provide immediate access to new features: You can leverage the latest help center enhancements as soon as they are released, without waiting for backward compatibility development.
  • Improve compliance: Newer API versions are hardened against modern web threats and address security and accessibility issues present in legacy versions.
  • Provide better support: Reducing the number of API versions allows our engineering and advocacy teams to troubleshoot and resolve your reported issues faster.

What do I need to do?

Check your help center templating version to determine the version you are currently using. You need to upgrade your help center theme to templating API v4 before July 31, 2027.

  • If you have developer resources: Your team can migrate your code using the ZCLI upgrade tool starting November 25, 2026. The right documentation will be provided later in a dedicated article.
  • If you prefer an automated visual tool: You can use the in-product GUI upgrade tool starting March 1, 2027, to upgrade with a few clicks and a manual QA check. 
  • If you use a Marketplace theme: Check with your theme developer to ensure you upgrade to a v4-ready version of the theme.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Release notes through 2026-09-11
articles.title: Release notes through 2026-09-11
articles.body:
See the What's New section for an overview of what was released last month.

This week's release notes include:

  • AI Agents
  • Knowledge
  • Apps and integrations
  • Contact Center
  • Products with no updates this week

AI Agents

Public - New

  • Additional Voice Locales: Colombian Spanish, Ecuadorian Spanish, Peruvian Spanish, Canadian English, Canadian French, Malay - Voice AI agents now support these locales with curated high-fidelity voices selected and validated with native speakers.
  • Voice Speed Control: Admins can now set how quickly the voice AI agent speaks using a speed slider on the agent. The setting applies to the whole agent and takes effect immediately on new conversations.
  • Calling recordings in Conversation Logs for Voice: Voice conversations now include call recordings you can listen to in Conversation logs.

Knowledge

New:

Help Center

  • We're moving from a GitHub OAuth App to a GitHub App. GitHub Apps provide more granular permissions, so we can request only the access needed to import themes instead of relying on broader repository access. This gives you greater control over which repositories and organizations the integration can access. See:
    • Setting up the GitHub integration with your help center theme
    • Troubleshooting your GitHub integration with help center themes

Fixed:

Editor

You can use the following content types within a callout:
  • Text
  • Block quotes
  • Images
  • Media (for example, video)
  • Tables
  • Horizontal lines

Contact Center

Fixed:

Contact Center

  • Fixed the issue where ringtone previews ignored the selected speaker device in Chrome. Ringtones now play through the selected wired or Bluetooth device.

Contact Center App

  • Fixed the end-of-call transcript comment being written before all agents had disconnected during multi-agent transfers. 
  • Fixed the incoming call ringtone continuing to play during agent whisper instead of stopping once a contact is accepted.
  • Fixed updating the API token or agent email from silently resetting Save Recording and Save Transcript settings.

Apps and integrations

New:
  • Transit (Theme)
    • Transit is a free transportation-focused Zendesk Help Center theme for transit agencies, rideshare, delivery, airlines, and travel platforms. It combines persistent sidebar navigation with a category grid, using high-contrast wayfinding, short reading paths, and monospace treatment for ticket numbers, booking references, and route codes. Colors, fonts, logos, hero text, layouts, page controls, and all 21 Guide page types are customizable without code; a free standard license is available, with a paid developer license adding code access and export.
  • Relay (Theme)
    • Relay is a free telecommunications-focused Zendesk Help Center theme for mobile carriers, broadband providers, MVNOs, and connectivity platforms. It uses persistent sidebar navigation to keep plans, billing, coverage, devices, outages, and troubleshooting one click away, with a lightweight design suited to customers browsing on mobile connections. Branding, fonts, logos, hero content, layout, page controls, and all 21 Guide page types are customizable without code; the standard license is free, and the developer license adds code access and export.
  • Artex (Theme)
    • Artex is a theme built for organizations that want a polished, professional customer support experience without sacrificing usability. It combines a strong visual identity with practical Help Center functionality. Customers can quickly search for answers, browse knowledge base content, participate in community discussions, and submit support requests through a consistent interface.
  • Vault (Theme)
    • A free financial-services-focused Zendesk Help Center theme for banks, fintechs, lenders, insurers, and payment platforms. It uses persistent sidebar navigation to keep accounts, access, payments, transfers, disputes, and security easy to access, with monospace styling for account numbers, amounts, and reference codes. The theme is fully customizable through Theming Center, responsive and WCAG AA focused, with a free standard license and optional paid developer license for code access and export.
  • Picto (Theme)
    • A free software-and-cloud-services Zendesk Help Center theme for SaaS companies, developer tools, APIs, and cloud platforms. It centers on persistent sidebar navigation so categories and sections remain visible while customers browse, making areas such as getting started, integrations, billing, and troubleshooting immediately accessible. Colors, fonts, logos, hero content, layouts, and all 21 Guide page types can be customized without code; the standard license is free, and the developer license adds code access and export.
  • backwise (Support)
    • backwise is a refund and return fraud-prevention platform for ecommerce merchants. It adds a Zendesk ticket-sidebar panel where agents can create claims with ticket and requester information, evaluate risk using conversation, order, carrier, and purchase/return history, inspect the reasoning behind the evaluation, and write the resulting verdict back to the ticket as a private note.
  • Choji (Support)
    • Choji is an AI-powered product and engineering workflow platform that turns Zendesk support conversations into customer evidence and potential engineering work. It continuously ingests tickets, public comments, and attachments, identifies bugs and feature requests, consolidates related customer reports, enriches existing engineering issues, and maintains traceability back to the originating Zendesk conversation.
  • Tag Janitor (Support)
    • Tag Janitor audits Zendesk ticket tags beyond the normal tag-management limits, showing ticket counts, usage, last-used information, where tags appear in triggers, automations, macros, views, SLAs, fields, and organizations, plus possible typos or case duplicates. It supports bulk rename, merge, and delete operations and highlights limitations around closed tickets, scan scope, and administrator permissions so teams can clean up tags without unintentionally breaking workflows.
  • Help Center Linker (Support)
    • Help Center Linker brings Help Center article discovery into the Zendesk ticket editor. Agents can search articles by keyword, preview results, insert formatted article links with one click, automatically receive localized results, and browse paginated results with section names without switching browser tabs.
  • TicketMind (Support)
    • TicketMind is an AI support engineer designed to diagnose complex customer issues faster. It reasons across Zendesk tickets, knowledge bases, previous resolutions, SOPs, databases, APIs, and SaaS systems to identify likely root causes and generate reviewable responses in Zendesk. It is designed to reduce resolution time, expand Tier 1 capabilities, protect engineering capacity, and turn successful resolutions into reusable knowledge.
  • Sentiment Stream (Support) (paid)
    • Sentiment Stream provides a live Zendesk triage board showing customer sentiment for active and recently closed conversations. Teams can sort and filter conversations by sentiment, change, duration, status, or group; see transcript-grounded explanations of sentiment changes; monitor average speed of answer and queue depth; identify queue-wait effects; and open conversations directly in Zendesk.
  • Sendrel (Support) (paid)
    • Sendrel lets agents forward selected Zendesk ticket comments to external recipients and automatically put replies back onto the original ticket as internal notes. Agents can send individual comments, ranges, or the full conversation; include attachments; optionally create editable summaries in several languages; and use a shared address book, while keeping the interaction visible on the ticket rather than in individual email inboxes.

Products with no updates this week

  • Admin Center
  • Support
  • Copilot
  • Voice
  • Analytics
  • Zendesk Workforce Management (WFM)
  • Zendesk QA
  • Mobile SDKs

articles.name: Service Incident - September 1, 2026 - Voice/Sales | Issues with Voice calls and call functions
articles.title: Service Incident - September 1, 2026 - Voice/Sales | Issues with Voice calls and call functions
articles.body:
Summary

On September 1, 2026, from 16:15 UTC to 18:26 UTC, Voice customers across fourteen US and EU pods experienced failures placing and receiving calls, along with degraded availability of call-related features, including hold, mute, voicemail, call greetings, digital calls, call recordings and transcriptions, Voice Settings, and Voice API requests. Sales Voice customers experienced similar degradation in call functionality during the incident window.

Timeline

September 1, 2026 17:22 UTC | September 1, 2026 10:22 AM PT

We are aware of an issue in the Voice product impacting inbound calls, outbound calls as well as call functions such as putting a call on hold.
 
We will provide updates as soon as they are available.

September 1, 2026 17:33 UTC | September 1, 2026 10:33 AM PT

Our teams are currently working with our telephony provider to restore all functionality within the Voice product. We will continue to provide updates with any new information. Thank you for your patience.

September 1, 2026 17:55 UTC | September 1, 2026 10:55 AM PT

We have increased the scope of this incident to include the impact to the Sales product with similar Voice product behavior Calls and Call functions may be impacted. Our telephony provider have now indicated to us that they are now monitoring recovery, and we see similar recovery in our own observability tools. We will provide an update when we are confident the issue is fully resolved.

September 1, 2026 18:26 UTC | September 1, 2026 11:26 AM PT

Our telephony provider has confirmed full recovery and both the Sales Voice features and Voice product should be fully operational once again. We do apologize for the interruption.

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by an issue with a security certificate update with our service provider. The update affected a service used to support calling, resulting in increased errors and failures for Voice and Sales Voice calls.

Resolution

To resolve the issue, our service provider rolled back the incorrectly configured security certificate deployment, restoring its REST API. We verified recovery through Voice and Sales Voice monitoring and confirmed that calling functionality had returned to normal.

Remediation Items

  1. Improve how quickly critical service issues are brought to the attention of the responsible response team.
  2. Add earlier warnings for calling disruptions and increased service errors.
  3. Work with the provider to confirm that measures to prevent a recurrence are implemented.
  4. Obtain and record the provider’s findings on the cause of the outage.
  5. Evaluate backup options for calling services to strengthen reliability during future disruptions.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system

articles.name: My AI agent suggestions don't appear in knowledge sources
articles.title: My AI agent suggestions don't appear in knowledge sources
articles.body:
Problem

Why did my AI agent bot provide information that wasn't explicitly stated in my crawled content?

Solution

Your AI agent can provide information that isn't explicitly written in your help center when your procedure contains a "Generate answer" step, with the free-text instruction that would contain, for example: "Provide general guidance on choosing a product".

To fix the behavior, improve the free-text instruction in your "Generate answer" step, so only pulled knowledge from your help center surfaces.

articles.name: I cannot solve a ticket with an AI agent action
articles.title: I cannot solve a ticket with an AI agent action
articles.body:
Problem

I created a trigger to solve a ticket on the knowledge response event from my AI agent. In AI agent settings, below AI agent actions > A knowledge answer is shared, I selected Solve ticket. I can see the action in the conversation log, but don't see the update on the ticket.

Cause

Two issues may have happened:

  • The ticket update did not meet Zendesk’s validation requirements, as an Assignee is required when solving a ticket

  • There may also have been a conflicting update, for example another process updating the ticket at the same time

Resolution steps

To solve the issue, follow these steps:

  1. Add an action for the AI agent actions > A knowledge answer is shared, so it assigns the ticket to a user or group before the status changes to Solved

  2. Confirm all your fields required to solve the ticket are also populated in those A knowledge answer is shared actions

  3. Review the order of actions in the AI agent flow. The recommended sequence is: Populate required ticket fields > Assign the ticket to the appropriate user or group > Update the ticket status to Solved

  4. Perform a test with your team and verify that no additional update happens at the same time within the ticket events 

If these actions run in a different order, the solve action may fail with a validation error or conflict.

articles.name: How often does a web crawler check external content, and is it configurable?
articles.title: How often does a web crawler check external content, and is it configurable?
articles.body:
Question

For ZOS environment, how frequently does the new web crawler engine checks for new information and updates and is there a way to customize the frequency setting?

Answer

The web crawler runs automatically based on the syncing frequency configured in your Knowledge search settings, with options for Daily, Weekly, Monthly, or Never (defaulting to Weekly).

Also, please note:

  • The sitemap’s changefreq value does not affect the crawl schedule.
  • A crawl-delay directive in the site’s robots.txt file is not respected by the crawler.
  • If a scheduled crawl cannot complete—for example, because the website is temporarily unavailable—the previously indexed content remains searchable, and Zendesk will retry periodically.

Frequency of web crawler recrawls when changes are made directly on a customer's website

Several updates to the web crawler include the ability to customize the frequency of the crawler: daily, weekly, monthly or never (just like AI Agents). Frequency is not impacted by any plan or operational factors. Admins can customize the syncing frequency for both new and existing crawlers directly in Knowledge search settings. 

When the crawl status is “partially completed,” it indicates that some pages set for crawling were not indexed for reasons such as page errors, access issues, timeouts, exceeding limits, or content not being detected.  In this case you may review the crawler summary or contact Zendesk Customer Support for troubleshooting help.

articles.name: Can authenticated end-user names be displayed in conversations logs?
articles.title: Can authenticated end-user names be displayed in conversations logs?
articles.body:
Question

Can authenticated end-user names be displayed instead of “Customer” in the AI Agent Conversation Logs when authentication is enabled?

Answer

This is not possible right now. The system currently shows Customer for both authenticated and unauthenticated users in the Conversation logs for AI Agents. You will only find the customer's name visible on the related Zendesk ticket.

articles.name: Can we enable AI agents to remember previous replies/conversations, feedback etc.?
articles.title: Can we enable AI agents to remember previous replies/conversations, feedback etc.?
articles.body:
Question

Regarding Memory-rich AI, can we enable AI agents to remember previous replies/conversations, feedback etc.?

Answer

Zendesk AI agents can remember previous interactions, replies, and feedback within an active conversation, enabling natural, context-aware, and adaptive responses. However, "memory" in this context is session-based and does not mean agents persistently track a user's full support history across separate conversations by default.

articles.name: An entity wasn't recognized in email conversations with AI
articles.title: An entity wasn't recognized in email conversations with AI
articles.body:
Issue symptom

I noticed that an entity wasn't recognized in conversations, named Order_Number and another REGEX entity. Customer needs help with order number entities not being recognized in email bot (AI agent).

Resolution

It's possible that:

  1. You updated the regex used for Order_Number in the entity after the conversation you looked at were created. For example, conversation examples were created on August 7th and 9th. However, your entities were updated on August 12th.

  2. In addition, it's an expected behavior that Regex entities would never match in some conversations. The Regex used in the entity expects the order ID to start with 1 followed by seven digits. If the order IDs in the conversation examples do not have that pattern, no match is possible.

articles.name: Is there a limit to the number of steps in the generative procedures of an email AI agent?
articles.title: Is there a limit to the number of steps in the generative procedures of an email AI agent?
articles.body:
Question

Is there a maximum number of steps in the generative procedures of an email bot? My procedure needs to acknowledge additions and changes for more than 6 steps, but the flow is only built up to the fourth step. The procedure should have more than 6 steps, but the flow only has 4 steps. How can I reach my goal?

Answer

No, there's no set limit to the number of steps in generative procedures for email AI agents.

If your procedure needs more than the initial four steps shown in the map:

  1. You can keep adding steps by using the free-text adjustment field in the procedure builder and selecting Update procedure.

  2. The system will update the map each time you make changes, so you can repeat this process until your procedure is complete.

articles.name: Understanding how Explore calculates metrics and why similar report results might not match
articles.title: Understanding how Explore calculates metrics and why similar report results might not match
articles.body:
When a number in an Explore report doesn’t match what you expect or if it differs from another report, there might be a mismatch between what you think you are measuring and what you are actually measuring. The difference may be caused by the dataset, metric, filters, date range, aggregation, or time settings.

What's my plan?
All Suites Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support with Explore Professional or Enterprise

Summary: ◀▼

Learn how report metrics are calculated so you can spot why similar Explore reports differ. The article explains how datasets, filters, date ranges, aggregation, time zones, business or calendar hours, and ticket changes like merges, deletions, and reopens can affect results. It also helps you compare averages, medians, and ticket status-based time metrics when numbers don’t match expectations.

When a number in an Explore report doesn’t match what you expect or if it differs from another report, there might be a mismatch between what you think you are measuring and what you are actually measuring. The difference may be caused by the dataset, metric, filters, date range, aggregation, or time settings.

This article explains at a high level how metrics work, how time-based metrics are measured, and how ticket changes impact reports. Having a better understanding of how things are measured and knowing what to look for, can help ensure your reports are consistent. It can also help you resolve mismatches or discrepancies between your expectations and your reports.

This article contains the following topics:

  • Understanding how metrics work and the parts of a report
  • Understanding how time-based metrics are measured in reports
  • Understanding how ticket changes impact reports and why numbers change
  • Summary of what to check when results don’t match expectations

Related articles

  • Metrics and attributes for Zendesk Support
  • Understanding datasets
  • Data refresh intervals for analytics
  • Understanding discrepancies between Explore reports and exports

Understanding how metrics work and the parts of a report

A metric is a measure, such as the number of tickets or the time to first reply. Explore applies an aggregation to the metric, such as count, sum, average, or median, to calculate the result. Metrics are retrieved from a dataset containing your Zendesk data.

If two or more similar reports return different results, any of the following might be different in the reports:
  • Datasets
  • Metrics or metric formulas
  • Filters or Date attributes
  • Aggregations
  • Types of records, such as tickets or ticket updates

Before investigating a difference, check that both reports use the same dataset, metrics, filters, and time zone settings.

Understanding how time-based metrics are measured in reports

Time-based metrics measure specific periods in a ticket’s lifecycle. They don’t all measure the same kind of waiting time. For example, first reply time measures the time from ticket creation to the first public agent reply, while requester wait time measures the time a ticket spends in the New, Open, and On-hold statuses.

If you're seeing discrepancies between your time-based reports, check the following:

  • In which statuses is duration counted?: Some metrics, such as Requester wait time measure time in specific requester-facing statuses. The time an agent spends working might be excluded by design. Check which ticket statuses the metric includes. For example, requester wait time includes time in the New, Open, and On-hold statuses and does not display data for any other ticket status.

    You can create a report using your chosen metric and the Ticket status attribute to help you see which statuses a specific status measures.

    See the following articles for more information about time-based metrics:

    • About native Support time duration metrics
    • About native Call time duration metrics
  • Business vs calendar hours: Many time metrics exist in both business and calendar time variants which give different results. Check which one your report uses and whether your schedules are configured.

    When you create a report, time-based metrics are clearly labelled as using business or calendar hours.

  • Averages can hide distribution: Averages can be affected by unusually high or low values. Compare the average and median when you want to understand whether a small number of tickets is influencing the result. The average shows the overall mean; the median shows the middle value when the results are ordered. See Choosing metric aggregators.

Make sure you understand the definitions for first reply time, full resolution time, requester wait time, and agent work time. See Explore metrics.

Understanding how ticket changes impact reports and why numbers change

Explore reflects the current state of your ticket history. When tickets are updated, merged, or deleted, metrics computed over that history change retrospectively. In addition, recently closed activity can take time to appear while data syncs. This is expected behavior, but it means a screenshot of last month’s report is not a reliable baseline for validating today’s report.

Understanding the behavior of merged, deleted, and closed tickets can help you understand the results you see in your reports and potentially solve any discrepancies between your reports. Check for the following:
  • Merged tickets: A merged ticket is closed and its conversation moves to a new ticket. Merging a ticket can affect reports because the original ticket and the ticket it was merged into may no longer represent separate conversations. Check the dataset and metric definition to understand how merged tickets are counted.
  • Deleted tickets: Deleted tickets aren’t included in the Tickets dataset. As a result, a report can return a different result if tickets were deleted after an earlier report was run.
  • Solved date versus updated-date: Some metrics use when an event occurred, while others use the ticket’s current state. For example, a report filtered by Ticket solved - Date may include tickets solved during the selected period, while the Solved tickets metric counts tickets that are currently solved or closed. A ticket that was solved and later reopened can therefore affect these reports differently.

Summary of what to check when results don’t match expectations

If results in your reports don’t match your expectations or if you see discrepancies among reports, you can check the following:

  • Are both reports using the same dataset,?
  • Are both reports using the same filters (including hidden or default filters) and the same date attributes?
  • Are both reports using the same metric, metric formula, and aggregation? For example, are both using average rather than median, or count rather than distinct count?
  • Are both reports using the same metric, metric formula, and aggregation? For example, are both using average rather than median, or count rather than distinct count?
  • If you're comparing reports generated by different users make sure that they have the same time zone and start of the week (based on the language of the user)
  • Are both reports using the same hours measurement. For example, is one report using calendar hours and the other using business hours?
  • Were any tickets merged, deleted, reopened, or otherwise changed during or after the report period?

If you still don’t understand your results or if the numbers still differ significantly after you’ve completed your checklist, contact Zendesk Customer Support and include:

  • The exported report or a screen recording
  • The dataset name
  • The exact metric, including its formula from the Metrics panel
  • Two or three example ticket IDs

articles.name: Scheduled Maintenance -  October 5-20, 2026 - Pod 15 - Analytics Data Migration
articles.title: Scheduled Maintenance -  October 5-20, 2026 - Pod 15 - Analytics Data Migration
articles.body:
Zendesk will perform critical maintenance which will impact data freshness for customers on Pod 15 at some time between October 5th and 20th.
 

Important Note

During this maintenance window, analytics and reporting data for Pod 15 accounts will not refresh. Real-time monitoring, live agent activity, and core support operations are not affected. No data will be lost. The change moves the analytics data hosting from the United States to Australia to support in-country data residency for Australian customers.
 

What is happening

Zendesk is migrating Pod 15 analytics data from our US instance to a new Australia-based instance. This is part of our investment in data locality for Australian customers, enabling analytics data to be hosted in-country.

To perform the migration safely, we need to pause writes of new analytics data to the current US instance, migrate the historical and new data to Australia, validate it, and then reconnect analytics services to the Australian instance. During this transition, some analytics and reporting features will show data that is not current.
 

Maintenance window

This window avoids end-of-month reporting and billing cycles. The migration cannot be rescheduled per customer - it is a coordinated Pod-wide cutover.
 

What is affected

The following analytics and reporting features will not refresh with new data during the window:

  • Explore: 8 of 29 datasets will show data that is not current. The affected datasets are:
    • Knowledge - Quick Answers
    • Knowledge - User session
    • Knowledge - Page efficiency
    • Chat - Messaging Goal Conversions
    • AI Agents - Essential
    • AI - Intelligent Triage
    • AI - Copilot auto assist
    • AI - Copilot suggestions
    • The remaining 21 Explore datasets continue to refresh normally.
  • HyperArc (Agentic Analytics): Analytics data will not refresh during the window.
  • OBP usage dashboards (Admin Center): Detailed usage drill-down tables will be temporarily hidden. The total consumption figure and summary tiles remain visible and accurate.
  • Automated Resolution forecasts: Forecast notifications may be based on data that is not current during the window. Other real-time usage notifications are not affected.
  • ZQA dashboards (Quality Assurance): Customer-facing analytics dashboards will show data frozen at the last refresh before the window. The "Last updated time" indicator on each dashboard shows when data was last refreshed.
     

What is NOT affected

  • Real-time monitoring (ZRA) - live agent activity, real-time analytics, and live dashboards continue to operate normally
  • Core support operations - ticketing, messaging, talk, chat, and agent workflows are fully operational
  • Historical data - all existing analytics data remains accessible
  • Billing and usage totals - total consumption figures remain accurate
  • 21 of 29 Explore datasets - refresh normally throughout
     

What customers need to do

  • No configuration changes are required.
  • If you have access to HyperArc but have not yet enabled it, please wait until after this maintenance window before enabling it, to avoid a confusing experience with non-current data.
  • After the window completes, allow time for data to backfill and validate. Reports and dashboards will return to normal refresh rates once the migration is complete and validated.
     

What to expect during the window

  • Dashboards and reports for affected features will display data that is not current, frozen at the last refresh before the migration began.
  • No error messages will be shown - dashboards remain accessible, but the data will not reflect recent activity.
  • Once the migration is complete and validated, all affected analytics services will reconnect to the Australian instance and resume normal refresh rates.
     

Why we are doing this

This migration enables Zendesk to host Pod 15 analytics data in Australia, supporting data locality requirements for Australian customers in regulated industries. After completion, analytics data for Pod 15 accounts will be stored in-country.
 

Questions or concerns

If you have questions, please contact Zendesk Support or your account representative. For status updates during the maintenance window, refer to status.zendesk.com.

articles.name: How can I set up geo blocking for my AI agent?
articles.title: How can I set up geo blocking for my AI agent?
articles.body:
Question

Can I set up geo blocking for my AI agent or bot widget? I'd like to set up geo blocking, so the French bot only appears to users with a French IP address for example. Is this possible?

Answer

No, you cannot block users geographically with AI agent and messaging settings.

Workarounds

However, you can use these workarounds instead:

Conditionally load the widget on the website

  • What it does: The customer’s site can perform an IP-geolocation check, then only inject/load the Zendesk widget for visitors located in France or another country

  • Considerations: Requires custom development and an IP geolocation provider or service, outside of your Zendesk configuration

Use CDN or WAF geo rules

  • What it does: Configure geographic restriction rules at your CDN or Web Application Firewall (WAF) level to filter traffic or restrict widget access based on visitor IP location at the network edge.

  • Considerations: This is best for stricter geographic controls, but is outside Zendesk configuration

Separate French language site or brand page

  • What it does: Add the French or language widget only to the French or language version of the site

  • Considerations: This is straightforward if you already have language or region-specific pages
